text.p: The Finnish markka was undervalued by as much as eight percent, based on long-term trade-weighted data at the end of the third quarter, and may firm to 2.95-2.90 German marks this year, Salomon Brothers said on Tuesday.
"The markka is undervalued," Salomon vice president and economist Wike Groenenberg told Reuters on a visit to Helsinki.
She based her view on the markka's level relative to its own long-term average, using GDP deflator-based and unit labour cost-based data provided by the European Community.

In a report on the overall economic outlook dated January 3, Salomon said the bias was for a slightly stronger markka , with the Bank of Finland possibly thwarting the unit's rise by cutting key rates to slightly below those in Germany.
"The currency is slightly undervalued on a trade-weighted basis, while prices of paper -- a key export market -- appear to have bottomed," Salomon said.
Finland's key interest rate, the tender rate, is currently level with Germany's repo rate at 3.0 percent.

In bonds, Finland seems to offer the largest scope for outperformance among the Nordic countries, Groenenberg said, expecting Finland's yield premium over Germany to virtually disappear by end-1997. On Tuesday, the premium was at about 36 basis points.
Increasing anticipation of Finland's entry into EMU would drive bonds, the Salomon report said.
"In contrast, investors likely will be increasingly persuaded that Denmark and Sweden will stay out of the euro zone for several years after its inauguration," it added.
